data.source: data/v2/cone_replicates_fsri.csv as of Oct 6 2026 (735 rows / 81 materials). Not modified by this round.
data.row_id: '<material>|<hf_tag>|R<replicate>', e.g. 'HDPE|HF25|R3'. Checked unique over all 735 rows (0 duplicates).
data.universe_U: rows with early_stop == False AND spark_ignitor == True: 723 rows / 79 materials (assert).
data.S681: U with did_not_ignite == False: 681 rows / 76 materials. Assert they are the same rows, in the same order, as v5.df (index-aligned), with y == v5.df['time_to_ignition_s'] exactly. Flux counts {15: 3, 25: 223, 35: 16, 50: 221, 75: 217, 100: 1}.
data.S675: S681 minus the 6 rows flagged by data_qa_decision.rule: 675 rows / 76 materials. Flux counts {15: 3, 25: 218, 35: 16, 50: 221, 75: 216, 100: 1} (assert). The 6 rows are removed from both training and scoring in every model and fold. They are never turned into censored rows.
data.C_censored: U with did_not_ignite == True: 42 rows / 8 materials (assert, and assert the id set equals censored_rows.ids). Used ONLY as right-censored training rows by a1 and a2. Never scored and never predicted for a metric.
data.excluded_DNI: PMMA|HF15-noSpark|R1, R2, R3 (spark_ignitor False: a no-spark protocol, while every scoring row is spark-ignited). Never used.
data.y: tti_s (seconds), float. All scoring rows are > 0 (assert).
data.censor_time: end_of_test_time_s (seconds from start of exposure, the same origin as tti_s) on the 42 C rows. Assert all 42 are finite and > 0. Right-censoring means the event time T > c.
data.groups: material, with no merges (76 groups on S681 and S675).
data.family_groups (reported-only protocol): v5 'family' rule: first token of material_props categories split on ';', stripped; missing -> 'unknown'. Computed for U, including the C rows.
data.features: PHYS = [log_q, log_dT, log_kpc, log_L, log_rho] in this order (v5.PHYS). Build them for all 723 U rows with v5's module-level tables and formulas: left-join v5.mcc, v5.mcc_x (onset-bc columns), v5.props and v5.thermal on material; then q = heat_flux_kWm2*1e3, dT = t_onset_C - 20, L = cone_thickness_mm/1e3, log_q = log(q), log_dT = v5.log_pos(dT), log_kpc = v5.log_pos(k_WmK*rhoc_Jm3K), log_L = v5.log_pos(L), log_rho = v5.log_pos(density_kgm3) (v5 lines 107-131). Assert np.array_equal(PHYS on S681, v5.df[v5.PHYS], equal_nan=True). Material-level PHYS inputs that are missing for the C materials (drafter's coverage check): Feather_Pillow_Feathers rho, kpc; Gypsum_Wallboard onset; Polyisocyanurate_Foam_Board kpc; Fiberglass_Insulation_R13_Paper_Faced rho, kpc; Fiberglass_Insulation_R30 onset, rho, kpc; Mineral_Wool_Insulation onset. They stay NaN and are handled by each model's own missing-value path.
data.leakage_guard: No feature reads tti_s, end_of_test_time_s, did_not_ignite, early_stop, test_status, replicate, test_date or post_test_cmt (v5's assert covers PHYS). end_of_test_time_s and did_not_ignite enter a1/a2 only as the censoring time and indicator of TRAINING rows.

censored_rows.rule: C = U with did_not_ignite True. This is the plan's 15 usable rows from benchmark materials plus the 27 never-ignite inert rows, with the 3 PMMA no-spark rows excluded.
censored_rows.fold_rule (the leakage trap): In fold k of repeat r, a C row enters training only if its material is NOT among that fold's test materials. So a benchmark material's own censored rows are always out of the fold in which it is tested. The 27 inert rows have no scoring row and are in training in every fold. Under family-GKF (reported only) the same rule uses family labels: a C row enters only if its family is not a test family in that fold.
censored_rows.fold_asserts: every fold, both row sets, both groupings: set(groups of included C rows) & set(test groups) == empty set. Log the number of included C rows per fold to the diagnostics file.

data_qa_decision.what: Should the 6 replicates whose FSRI operator comment says TTI is invalid or was shortened be scored and trained on (S681), or dropped (S675)? Both versions are computed and reported. Arnav names the canonical set under D4 before step 1 runs, on the comment text alone, i.e. before he or anyone sees any score in this round (including exp046 on 675 rows). If D4 approves the round but names no set, the round is BLOCKED; the executor never picks.

rule (text only; Python re, re.IGNORECAS.meaning: The operator says the recorded TTI is invalid, or was shortened, faster or reduced, e.g. by specimen-igniter contact. Comments saying contact did NOT affect TTI are kept (ABS|HF75|R1, HIPS|HF25|R3 match NEG).

data_qa_decision.asserts (label-free, step 0): On all 735 rows the rule flags exactly flagged_ids, and all 6 are in S681. PET|HF25|R1 is NOT flagged: its comment only says the mass data were affected. The drafter ran this regex on Oct 6: POS matched 6 rows, NEG 2 rows, overlap 0, and the flagged set equals flagged_ids.
data_qa_decision.canonical_S681: exp046 as on record is the incumbent. S675 results are reported only.
data_qa_decision.canonical_S675: The exp046 pipeline re-scored on S675 becomes the TTI number of record whichever way it moves (snapshot-rule style, as loi_snapshot_update2), after the critic. It is also the incumbent for adoption in this round. exp046's 0.3133 on 681 rows stays as history in the record note. S681 results are reported only.
data_qa_decision.scope_of_rule: From Arnav's D4 decision on, every NEW run that trains or scores a model on FSRI tti_s labels uses the canonical set and states it: this round, the round-9 TabPFN tti_arm if run, plan A4 conformal TTI intervals, demo/predict.py's TTI model, and plan A2's FSRI-trained exp046. This config does not amend other configs: if S675 becomes canonical, a committed config that fixes 681 rows and has not yet scored (e.g. macfp_wood_crosslab.json, whose step 1 reproduces exp046 on 681 rows) is amended by the orchestrator, before its first score, to use S675; with no amendment it runs as committed and labels its TTI output '681 rows, pre-D4 definition'. Outputs made earlier are not re-run, except where their own config says so (conformal_intervals.json: re-run unchanged if 675 becomes canonical), and stay labelled 681 rows; tti_secondary_metrics.json is declared on 681 rows and stays so. pHRR, THR, FIGRA and Char Residue are not TTI labels and keep these 6 replicates (see open_questions).
data_qa_decision.not_in_rule (declared, NOT applied): Other TTI-related comments seen while drafting describe a LATE-recorded TTI, which biases the other way: Black_PMMA|HF75|R4 (1-2 s human delay), Latex_Pillow_Foam|HF75|R1 and |R3 (actual ignition < 2 s), Wood_Stud|HF25|R3 (actual about 110-115 s), Nylon|HF25|R2 and |R3 (recorded when flame began spreading), Nylon_Carpet_High_Pile|HF25|R1 (recorded more than a minute after initial ignition). The HDPE material.json note that HF25 R5/R6 used 60 mm spacing is also not in the rule. The plan's decision covers the 6 shortened/invalid rows only. Adding any of these would create a third row set and needs an amendment before any score (see open_questions).

folds.primary: For each row set separately (S681, S675) and r = 0..9: GroupKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=r).split(X_S, y_S, groups_S), exactly as eval_protocol.repeated_group_kfold. Every model uses the same splits, so comparisons are paired. Folds are recomputed on S675; nothing carries over from S681.
folds.custom_loop: All models run through one loop, rgkf_censored(model, X_S, y_S, g_S, X_C, c_C, g_C), whose splitting code is a copy of eval_protocol.repeated_group_kfold. It hands the fold's admissible C rows (censored_rows.fold_rule) to a1 and a2 through fit(X, y, X_cens, c_cens); every other model gets fit(X, y). Predictions are written to oof[r, te].
folds.identity_check (step 1): For exp046 on S681 and on S675, the loop's (10, n) OOF array must be np.array_equal to eval_protocol.repeated_group_kfold(model, X, y, groups)[1]. Otherwise BLOCKED.
folds.family_gkf (reported only): the same loop with groups = family labels on the scoring rows, r = 0..9.

incumbent.estimator: v5.linear(PoissonRegressor(alpha=0.01, max_iter=3000)) on PHYS, raw seconds
incumbent.on_S675: the same pipeline re-scored on S675 in step 2 (no reference value). If S675 is canonical, it is the incumbent here and the tracker assigns it a new exp id.

candidates (config order = tie order; no.role: CONTROL, never selectable: lognormal AFT on ignited rows only. With no censored rows it is a ridge-penalised Gaussian regression of log t on PHYS, predicted on the seconds scale. It isolates what a1's censored rows add.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.preprocessing: SimpleImputer(strategy='median', add_indicator=True) then StandardScaler(), the v5.linear pipeline without its estimator. Fit on the fold's ignited training rows only (the same in a0 and a1, so a1 - a0 isolates the censored likelihood terms). Gives Xs with p = 5 + number of indicator columns. A feature missing at transform but not at fit is median-filled with no indicator (sklearn 1.7.1 SimpleImputer uses error_on_new=False; checked by the drafter).
candidates (config order = tie order; no.training_rows: ignited training rows of the fold (n_ign rows)
candidates (config order = tie order; no.likelihood (Olsen parameterisation): w = (g0, g_1..g_p, th), th > 0; sigma = 1/th, mu = (g0 + Xs.g)/th. Ignited row i, l_i = log(y_i): r_i = th*l_i - g0 - Xs_i.g; nll_i = -log(th) + 0.5*r_i^2 (constants l_i + 0.5*log(2*pi) dropped).
candidates (config order = tie order; no.objective: F(w) = sum_i nll_i / n_ign + 0.5*0.01*sum_k g_k^2. g0 and th are not penalised. alpha 0.01 and the 1/n scaling copy exp046's PoissonRegressor (sklearn minimises mean deviance/2 = mean NLL plus alpha/2 ||w||^2). F is convex on th > 0, so the optimum is unique and the start does not matter.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.gradient (analytic): dF/dg0 = -sum r_i / n_ign; dF/dg = -sum r_i Xs_i / n_ign + 0.01*g; dF/dth = sum(-1/th + r_i l_i) / n_ign.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.start: [b0, b] = numpy.linalg.lstsq([1, Xs], l, rcond=None)[0] on the fold's ignited training rows; s0 = sqrt(mean(residual^2)); w0 = (b0/s0, b/s0, 1/s0).
candidates (config order = tie order; no.optimizer: scipy.optimize.minimize(F, w0, jac=True, method='L-BFGS-B', bounds=[(None, None)]*(p+1) + [(1e-8, None)], options={'maxiter': 20000, 'maxfun': 200000, 'ftol': 1e-13, 'gtol': 1e-9}). One run, no restarts.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.converged: res.success is True, or max|grad F(res.x)| <= 1e-5. Predictions always use res.x, converged or not (a non-converged fit still predicts; it only removes its candidate from 'selectable', see adoption).
candidates (config order = tie order; no.prediction: pred = min(exp(mu + sigma^2/2), cap_fold): the lognormal mean, with sigma = this fit's single global MLE sigma. This is the plan's 'mean exp(mu + s^2/2), with sigma declared up front': one global sigma, mean not median, no stratification.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.cap_fold: max(y) over the fold's ignited training rows: the data-tied cap from the tti_round1 critic (caveat 3). Applied to a0, a1 and a2 alike so the AFT family is comparable. Not applied to exp046, o1 or o2.

candidates (config order = tie order; no.role: selectable: a0 plus right-censored non-ignition rows
candidates (config order = tie order; no.preprocessing: exactly a0's: imputer and scaler fit on the fold's ignited training rows, then applied to the admissible C rows
candidates (config order = tie order; no.training_rows: the fold's ignited training rows plus admissible C rows (censored_rows.fold_rule): up to 42, of which the 27 inert rows are always included
candidates (config order = tie order; no.likelihood: a0's terms for ignited rows, plus for each censored row j with k_j = log(c_j): s_j = g0 + Xs_j.g - th*k_j; nll_j = -scipy.special.log_ndtr(s_j), i.e. -log P(T > c_j).
candidates (config order = tie order; no.objective: F(w) = (sum_i nll_i + sum_j nll_j) / n_ign + 0.5*0.01*sum_k g_k^2. The divisor is n_ign, the ignited training rows, as in a0, so a1 = a0 + censored terms exactly. Still convex.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.gradient (analytic): lambda(s) = exp(scipy.stats.norm.logpdf(s) - log_ndtr(s)) (inverse Mills ratio, computed in log space). Censored contributions: dF/dg0 += -sum lambda_j / n_ign; dF/dg += -sum lambda_j Xs_j / n_ign; dF/dth += sum lambda_j k_j / n_ign.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.start: a0's start (OLS on the ignited training rows only)
candidates (config order = tie order; no.prediction: as a0: min(exp(mu + sigma^2/2), cap_fold), sigma = this fit's global MLE sigma
candidates (config order = tie order; no.extra_adoption_condition: see adoption.round_specific R1 (a1 must beat a0)

candidates (config order = tie order; no.role: selectable: HGB Poisson with the exact thermally-thick theory offset
candidates (config order = tie order; no.estimator: HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss='poisson', **v5.HGB) = learning_rate 0.05, max_iter 300, max_leaf_nodes 15, min_samples_leaf 20, l2_regularization 1.0, random_state 0. Every other argument is the sklearn 1.7.1 default (early_stopping 'auto' is off for n < 10000).
candidates (config order = tie order; no.features: PHYS, NaN-native, no imputation. log_q stays a feature so the trees can learn the near-critical upturn.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.wrapper: class OffsetPoissonHGB(BaseEstimator, RegressorMixin). q_kW = numpy.round(exp(X[:, 0]) / 1000, 6) (X[:, 0] = log_q = log(1000*q_kW); the rounding undoes the float round-trip, e.g. exp(log(50000))/1000 = 50.00000000000001, so q_kW equals heat_flux_kWm2 exactly and o is exactly 1.0 at 50 kW/m2); o = (50/q_kW)^2. fit(X, y): hgb.fit(X, y * (q_kW/50)^2, sample_weight=o). predict(X): hgb.predict(X) * o. This is exactly a Poisson log-link model with offset log o = -2 log(q/50).
candidates (config order = tie order; no.check: once, on the full U table: np.array_equal(numpy.round(exp(log_q)/1000, 6), heat_flux_kWm2) (every flux in the table is a whole kW/m2: 15, 25, 35, 50, 75, 100)
candidates (config order = tie order; no.coefficient: -2 on log q'' comes from thermally-thick ignition theory. It is fixed, never estimated, never varied. The data median -2.08 is NOT its source.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.training_rows: ignited training rows only (no censored rows)

candidates (config order = tie order; no.role: selectable: equal average of the incumbent and o1
candidates (config order = tie order; no.estimator: train_blend_round1.Avg([v5.linear(PoissonRegressor(alpha=0.01, max_iter=3000)), OffsetPoissonHGB()]), raw seconds, equal weights

candidates (config order = tie order; no.role: selectable unless Arnav drops it under D4 (default: included): lognormal AFT with a learned, capped critical heat flux, t = A(x) / (q'' - q_cr(x))^2, trained with the censored rows
candidates (config order = tie order; no.material_features: Z = [log_dT, log_kpc, log_L, log_rho] (PHYS without log_q). Imputer + indicators + StandardScaler as in a0, fit on the fold's ignited training rows, applied to admissible C rows. Gives Zs with p_z columns.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.parameters: w = (a, b_1..b_pz, c, d_1..d_pz, eta); sigma = exp(eta)
candidates (config order = tie order; no.structure: q in kW/m2, taken from X[:, 0] exactly as o1's wrapper does: q = numpy.round(exp(X[:, 0]) / 1000, 6), which equals heat_flux_kWm2 (o1.check); Z = X[:, 1:5]. a2 receives the same PHYS matrix as every model, plus the admissible C rows' PHYS and censor times. p_i = expit(c + Zs_i.d); qcr_i = QCAP * p_i with QCAP = 13.5 kW/m2; e_i = q_i - qcr_i; m_i = a + Zs_i.b - 2*log(e_i). log A = a + Zs.b. The exponent -2 is from theory and is never varied.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.QCAP: 13.5 kW/m2 = 0.9 x 15 kW/m2, the lowest heat flux among the scoring rows (a design setting). Every scoring and censored row has q >= 15, so e >= 1.5 kW/m2 always and every log-likelihood term is finite. Consequence, declared now: a2 cannot predict 'never ignites', and the largest TTI(25)/TTI(50) ratio it can express is ((50-13.5)/(25-13.5))^2 = 10.07.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.likelihood: ignited: z_i = (l_i - m_i)/sigma, nll_i = eta + 0.5*z_i^2. Censored (admissible C rows): s_j = (m_j - log c_j)/sigma, nll_j = -log_ndtr(s_j).
candidates (config order = tie order; no.objective: F(w) = (sum nll_i + sum nll_j) / n_ign + 0.5*0.01*(sum b^2 + sum d^2). a, c and eta are not penalised. F is not convex, so the single declared start below is part of the model.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.gradient (analytic): dm/da = 1; dm/db = Zs; dm/dqcr = 2/e; dqcr/dc = QCAP*p*(1-p); dqcr/dd = QCAP*p*(1-p)*Zs. Ignited: dnll/dm = -z/sigma, dnll/deta = 1 - z^2. Censored: dnll/dm = -lambda(s)/sigma, dnll/deta = lambda(s)*s, with lambda as in a1. Then divide by n_ign and add the penalty gradients 0.01*b and 0.01*d.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.start: c0 = 0, d0 = 0 (q_cr = QCAP/2 = 6.75 kW/m2 for every row); [a_start, b_start] = numpy.linalg.lstsq([1, Zs], l + 2*log(q - 6.75), rcond=None)[0] over the fold's ignited training rows; eta_start = log(sqrt(mean(residual^2))) with residual = l + 2*log(q - 6.75) - (a_start + Zs.b_start).
candidates (config order = tie order; no.optimizer: scipy.optimize.minimize(F, w0, jac=True, method='L-BFGS-B', options={'maxiter': 20000, 'maxfun': 200000, 'ftol': 1e-13, 'gtol': 1e-9}), no bounds. One run, no restarts.
candidates (config order = tie order; no.prediction: pred = min(exp(m + sigma^2/2), cap_fold), cap_fold as a0
candidates (config order = tie order; no.diagnostics_reported: per fit: min/median/max of fitted qcr over the test rows, sigma, converged, n_iter

candidates_not_run: Smearing of any member; b2 or ExtraTrees variants; stratified-sigma or median-prediction AFT variants; an a2 without censored rows; other QCAP/start/cap values; per-material q_crit (impossible under GKF: a held-out material has none, tti_round1); emissivity; any feature beyond PHYS.

adoption.primary_rows: the canonical set named under D4 (S681 or S675)
adoption.family (adoption_gate_v2 'family'): [a0, a1, o1, o2, a2] in this order: K = 5, or K = 4 if Arnav drops a2. If Arnav also approves round9_tabpfn_smearing.json's tti_arm under D4, its p1 and p2 join after a2 (K up to 7). They are scored on the same canonical rows with identical splits, and the TTI adoption decision waits until every member is scored. a0 is a control: it counts in K and is never selectable. Cross-config precondition if the tti_arm runs: adoption_gate_v2 definitions.order sorts configs by plan item label (B2 before B4), which would put p1, p2 first, while this config and round9_tabpfn_smearing.json (adoption.families.TTI) both put them after a2. The order only breaks exact ties and fills the npz 'order' array, but it must be single-valued: the D4 amendment, recorded in both configs before any TTI score, states the order the gate uses and that this config's TTI output names govern (outputs.oof_and_gate). Without that amendment the tti_arm is BLOCKED (FLAG) and the B4 family runs alone.
adoption.selectable: a1, o1, o2, a2 (and p1, p2 if the tti_arm runs), MINUS any candidate with a non-converged fit (see 'converged') among its 50 primary-row fits. Non-convergence is known before any R2 is computed, so this is not a score-based choice. Such a candidate is still scored, reported and counted in K.
adoption.selection: the selectable member with the highest repeated-GKF mean on the primary rows, at full precision; exact ties go to the first in family order. Only that candidate is tested. There is no fallback to the second-best.
adoption.rule_in_force: Fixed from Arnav's D1 answer, quoted under 'amendments', before any score. D1 approved -> rule A. D1 explicitly declined, and this config approved under D4 -> rule B. D1 unanswered -> BLOCKED (adoption_gate_v2.json scope.if_D1_pending_or_declined). The executor never picks the rule.
adoption.rule_A_if_D1_approved: experiments/configs/adoption_gate_v2.json exactly. G1: wins >= 8/10, strict. G2: repeat-0 ci_lo >= the incumbent's repeat-0 ci_lo as computed in this run on the primary rows. G3: studentised max-T paired group-bootstrap lower bound of the repeat-mean gain > 0 (B 2000, seed 0, draws identical to eval_protocol.bootstrap_ci, ddof 1, linear 0.95 quantile, over the whole family). If the approved gate file differs from this summary, the approved file governs.
adoption.rule_B_if_D1_declined: the current rule (tti_round2 / blend_round1): adopt only if wins >= 8/10 strictly better than the incumbent AND repeat-0 ci_lo >= the incumbent's (0.0715 published, if S681 canonical; the run's re-baselined exp046 ci_lo, if S675 canonical). The gate_v2 quantities are still computed and reported, report-only.

round_specific.R1: If the selected candidate is a1, it is NOT adopted when rkf_mean(a0) >= rkf_mean(a1) on the primary rows: then censoring added nothing, and a0 is a control that can never be adopted. (Mirrors tti_round2's e4 identity-control clause.)
round_specific.R2: Any non-finite OOF prediction in any family member on the primary rows -> FLAG (blocker file), no adoption decision (adoption_gate_v2 exit_triggers).

adoption.then: critic pass in a fresh context before numbers_of_record.json changes. The critic may block for a bug; it may not adopt a candidate that failed the rule in force. Only the orchestrator edits numbers_of_record / trackers (scripts/update_trackers.py).
adoption.non_canonical_rows: Everything above is also computed on the non-canonical row set for exp046, a0, a1, o1, o2 and a2, and reported. The round-9 tti_arm members p1/p2 run on the canonical rows only (round9_tabpfn_smearing.json tti_arm.rows). Non-canonical numbers never select, adopt, demote or change wording of the record.

procedure (in order; each step's stop ru: Step 0, label-free: build U, S681, S675, C and PHYS; every assert in data, censored_rows and data_qa_decision, plus o1.check; self_tests T1-T4; if the tti_arm is approved, confirm the adoption.family amendment is recorded (else that arm is BLOCKED). Any other failure -> FLAG (blocker), stop.

Step 1: exp046 on S681 through eval_protocol.repeated_group_kfold + bootstrap_ci(y, oof[0], groups) must give rkf_mean 0.3133 +-0.002 and CI [0.0715, 0.4958] +-0.002, else BLOCKED. Then folds.identity_check on S681.
Step 2: exp046 on S675 (re-baseline, always computed) and folds.identity_check on S675.
Step 3: a0, a1, o1, o2, a2 (a2 unless dropped) on S681 and on S675, each through rgkf_censored with its own row set's splits. Save every (10, n) OOF array.
Step 4: family-GKF for exp046 and every candidate on both row sets (reported only).

Step 5: the adoption rule in force on the primary rows only. If rule A, run adoption_gate_v2 exactly per its implementation block, after every family member (including tti_arm members, if any) is scored.
Step 6: reported_only quantities; write outputs; FLAG blocker summarising the round for Arnav; critic in a fresh context before any number from this round is quoted or any record changes.

self_tests_label_free (synthetic data on.T1_gradients: rng = numpy.random.default_rng(0), n = 500, draws in this order: X = rng.normal(size=(500, 3)); l = 5 + X @ [0.5, -0.3, 0.2] + 0.6 * rng.normal(size=500); q = rng.choice([15.0, 25.0, 50.0, 75.0], size=500); cens = rng.random(500) < 0.10 (these rows are censored at c = exp(l)); then X[rng.random((500, 3)) < 0.10] = nan. Preprocessing exactly as a0 (imputer + indicators + scaler fit on the non-censored rows). a1 uses the 3 columns (+ indicators) as Xs; a2 uses them as Zs, with q. Points: each model's declared start w0, then 3 points w0 + 0.1 * rng.normal(size=w0.size), drawn after the data, a1's three then a2's three. At each point, scipy.optimize.check_grad(F, gradF, w) (default epsilon) / ||gradF(w)|| < 1e-5.
self_tests_label_free (synthetic data on.T2_aft_recovery: rng = numpy.random.default_rng(1), n = 20000, draws in this order: X = rng.normal(size=(20000, 3)); eps = rng.normal(size=20000); l = 5 + 0.5 x1 - 0.3 x2 + 0.2 x3 + 0.6 eps. a1 part: rows with l > 5.3 are censored at c = exp(5.3) (about 36%); preprocessing fit on the non-censored rows as declared; penalty set to 0. Compare on the RAW feature scale: slope_k = g_k / (th * scaler.scale_[k]) and sigma = 1/th; pass if every |slope_k - true_k| < 0.03 and |sigma - 0.6| < 0.03. (The standardized-scale slopes g_k/th are not comparable: the scaler is fit on non-censored rows, where x1's SD is about 0.9.) a0 part: the same X and l with no censoring, preprocessing fit on all 20000 rows, penalty 0: g/th equals the OLS slopes of l on [1, Xs], g0/th the OLS intercept, and 1/th the OLS residual SD (ddof 0), each within 1e-6.
self_tests_label_free (synthetic data on.T3_a2_reaches_truth: rng = numpy.random.default_rng(2), n = 2000, draws in this order: Z = rng.normal(size=(2000, 2)); q = rng.choice([15.0, 25.0, 50.0, 75.0], size=2000); eps = rng.normal(size=2000). True raw-scale parameters a = 10.0, b = (0.5, -0.3), c = 0.0, d = (1.0, -0.5), sigma = 0.4: l = a + Z.b - 2*log(q - 13.5*expit(c + Z.d)) + 0.4*eps; rows with l > log(600) are censored at 600 s (about 8%), the rest are ignited. Preprocessing fit on the ignited rows; penalty 0.01 as declared; a2's declared start and optimizer. F(true) is evaluated at the true parameters mapped to the standardized coordinates: b_s = b * scale_, a_s = a + b.mean_, d_s = d * scale_, c_s = c + d.mean_, eta = log(0.4). Pass if the fit converges and F(fit) <= F(true) + 1e-6.
self_tests_label_free (synthetic data on.T4_offset_identity: rng = numpy.random.default_rng(3), n = 500: X = numpy.column_stack([numpy.full(500, log(50000.0)), rng.normal(size=(500, 4))]); y = exp(3 + 0.5 * X[:, 1] + 0.3 * rng.normal(size=500)). OffsetPoissonHGB (with its rounded q_kW) gives predictions np.array_equal to HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss='poisson', **v5.HGB) fit without sample_weight on the same X, y. Without the rounding in the wrapper this check fails (o = 0.9999999999999998 at 50 kW/m2; relative differences about 1.6e-15).
self_tests_label_free (synthetic data on.provenance: The skeptic ran T1-T4 exactly as specified here on synthetic data only (session scratchpad b4skeptic/t123.py, t4.py), with a straightforward implementation of the declared a1/a2 objectives and gradients: all pass (T1 relative errors 5.6e-8 to 7.6e-7; T2 raw-scale slopes 0.499 / -0.300 / 0.201, sigma 0.602; T3 converged, F(fit) -0.4013 <= F(true) -0.3962; T4 equal). No Dravix data was used.

seeds: GroupKFold random_state 0..9 (primary and family-GKF); bootstrap_ci n_boot 2000, seed 0; HGB random_state 0; self-test rng seeds 0, 1, 2, 3 (T1-T4). The AFT fits and the GLM are deterministic. There is no other randomness.

reported_only (never used to select, ado.top_k_removal: per candidate c on the primary rows: contribution of material m = sum over its rows i of mean_r[(y_i - oof_inc[r,i])^2 - (y_i - oof_c[r,i])^2]. Rank materials by contribution, descending (ties by name). For k in (1, 3, 5), drop the top-k materials' rows and report the mean over r of [R2_c - R2_inc] on the remaining rows and wins/10. These rows are never scored; this shows only whether the model puts their ignition beyond the cap. A table, no R2.

expected (not scored; plan and findings: Round effect 0 to +0.04 (0.31-0.35). o1 about 0.25-0.33; o2 0 to +0.03 vs 0.313 (models-tti-thick-offset). a1 vs a0: small, because 27 of 42 censored rows are trivial inerts. The 6-row QA change is of order 0.01 at most (fsri-tti-operator-flag-qa), though the Overstuffed_Chair_Polyester_Fabric row is the largest label error.
honesty_notes: Censor times are operator caps (30 min for R1, then 10 min for R2/R3 once R1 showed no mass loss). Short ones carry little information.

Feather_Pillow_Feathers HF25: 3 censored at 180-249 s, while its sibling ignited at 4 s. Polyisocyanurate_Foam_Board HF25: 1 of 4 did not ignite, with siblings at 2-3 s. House_Wrap HF50: 2 of 3 did not ignite; the lone ignition was at 34 s. Mixed cells like these inflate a global lognormal sigma, and the mean prediction exp(mu + sigma^2/2) then biases every AFT prediction upward. This config keeps the global-sigma mean deliberately (the plan's wording) and does not try alternatives.

27 of the 42 censored rows are never-ignite inerts whose onset/rho/kpc are partly NaN, so their signal lands on the missing-value indicators. A test material with the same missingness can then get a large prediction: Gypsum_Wallboard ignites at 50/75 and lacks onset like Fiberglass_R30 and Mineral_Wool. That is why the data-tied cap covers a0/a1/a2. The plan text names a cap only for a2; see choices.
a2's QCAP below 15 kW/m2 means it cannot represent materials that never ignite at 25 kW/m2 (PC, Gypsum, House_Wrap) as non-igniting, only as slow (ratio <= 10.07 vs 50 kW/m2).

o1 is the third HGB-Poisson form tried on TTI. The other two scored below exp046 (t3 0.212, e3 0.157). With fluxes almost all at 25/50/75, the offset mainly re-weights the loss (25 kW/m2 rows x4, 75 kW/m2 x0.44) and shares material structure across fluxes (models-tti-thick-offset verdict).

The 675-row option removes only rows whose TTI is biased LOW (shortened by igniter contact). Late-recorded rows, biased HIGH, stay. This one-sided cleaning is a known asymmetry, disclosed here, not corrected.

The 6 flagged rows were identified with their TTI values and sibling values in view (prior_looks). The regex is text-only, but it was written after the 6 rows were known, and it was checked to match exactly them.
The per-flux and log metrics are report-only and post hoc (tti_secondary_metrics.json). No number from this round is set against 0.58.
One material set (FSRI) and one lab: R2 here measures the flux response plus material separation, and the 25 kW/m2 rows hold 85% of the target SS (tti-1).
